h1: How Much Does Attic Insulation Cost in the East Bay?
description: What drives attic insulation cost in the East Bay: size, condition, material and R-value. Get your exact number with a free inspection and written estimate.
intro: Attic insulation cost in the East Bay follows the size of the attic, the condition of what is up there now, and the R-value target. Because those three things differ from house to house, there is no useful single number. The free inspection measures your attic and turns the drivers into an exact, fixed estimate.
author: East Bay Insulation

paragraphs: Five things move the price of an attic insulation job. Attic size is the biggest one, then condition, material, R-value and access.
bullets: Attic size: square footage sets the material quantity
Condition: clean attics cost less than ones with damaged or compacted insulation
Material: fiberglass, cellulose and spray foam carry different material costs
R-value target: deeper insulation means more material
Access: steep roofs, tight hatches and awkward layouts add labor time

paragraphs: Healthy old insulation can often stay and be topped up to the target depth, which keeps the job smaller and faster. Old insulation has to come out when it is compressed, damp, moldy or full of rodent droppings. Removal adds vacuum truck time and disposal, and it is the largest single add-on on many East Bay jobs, because marine-layer moisture and older houses make damaged insulation common.
bullets: Top-up: only possible when the existing material is dry and sound
Removal: required for damp, compacted or rodent-damaged material
The inspection tells you which path your attic needs

paragraphs: Blown-in fiberglass or cellulose is the common choice for open, vented attics: it covers the floor quickly and reaches high R-values at a lower material cost per inch. Spray foam costs more per inch, but it insulates and air seals in one pass, so it earns its place in unvented attics, low-slope roofs, rim joists and anywhere air and moisture move through the structure.
bullets: Spray foam suits unvented spaces and hard-to-air-seal areas
We recommend based on the house, not a product list

paragraphs: East Bay attics deal with marine-layer moisture near the bay and dry summer heat inland, often in houses built decades ago with little or no air sealing. Moisture shortens the life of attic insulation, so a damp or moldy layer is more common here than in drier climates, and ventilation checks matter as much as material choice.
bullets: Marine-layer moisture speeds up insulation wear
Older East Bay homes often need air sealing first
Ventilation and moisture readings are part of the inspection

sections.h2: How to get an exact number
paragraphs: The only way to price an attic accurately is to look at it. The free inspection measures the attic, checks the condition of the existing insulation, reads moisture levels and confirms access. You get a written estimate with a fixed price for your attic, not a range borrowed from another house.
bullets: Written estimate with a fixed price
